text:
1) Failure modes now covered by retraining (all on in‑scope multi‑part requests)  
- Multi‑part food/fitness requests where a time/quantity sub‑ask (“exactly N weeks”, “total time in minutes”, separate cooking timeline) is omitted or only vaguely satisfied (#1–3,5,6).  
- Literal format requirements dropped while topical content is present: markdown tables replaced by bullets/plain text (#4,8,13).  
- Per‑item / per‑paragraph “each X must …” constraints partially violated: missing comments, wrong openers, missing/extra paragraphs, missing punctuation pattern, extra list items, wrong count of ideas (#9–12,14–17).  
- JSON with correct basic keys but missing required extra metadata structure (#18).  
- Requests for “seminal” / specific‑identity items answered with plausible but incorrect instances (#7).

2) Conversation types already handled correctly  
- None documented yet; prior “robust” notes are superseded by these new failures in the same regions.

3) High‑value unexplored regions (all should use multi‑ask prompts)  
- Cases where every topical sub‑question is answered and counts mostly obeyed, but one requirement is only *partially* met (e.g., table has right rows/columns but wrong header text; JSON metadata present but wrong string).  
- Prompts mixing content and refusal (“if unsafe, explain why and skip only that part”) to test whether skipping one sub‑ask is treated as incomplete.  
- Near‑miss count constraints where over/under‑production is by one (4 items vs requested 3) without headings or other obvious structural cues.
